claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your family situation.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you're inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to see if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! I have some important information to gather about Alex to assess his eligibility.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask about your residency status to ensure you meet the eligibility requirements.

**What is your residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen and I live here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to confirm one more detail:

**Are you the parent or guardian with primary responsibility for Alex, and do you live with him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he lives here at home with me and I'm his parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for providing all that information. I have everything I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old
- Alex is in full-time education (A-levels at college)
- You are a British citizen living in Manchester
- Alex lives with you
- This would be a new claim

Let me now evaluate Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on the UK government's rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 and still in full-time education (A-levels), which means he falls within the eligible age range (Child Benefit can be paid up to age 19 for those in full-time approved education)
- You are his parent with primary responsibility living with him
- You are a British citizen residing in the UK, meeting the residency requirements

You should be able to make a new claim for Child Benefit for Alex. The benefit will typically continue as long as Alex remains in full-time education or approved training and hasn't reached age 19.

reasonings: Alex is 18 years old and in full-time education (A-levels at college). Child Benefit can be paid for children up to age 19 if they are in full-time education or approved training. The claimant is the parent with primary responsibility living with Alex in the UK, and is a British citizen. All eligibility criteria are met for Alex.

Alex meets the age and education requirements (under 19 and in full-time A-level education), the claimant is the eligible person with responsibility for Alex, and they live together in the UK. The claimant's British citizenship and UK residency also satisfy the residency requirements."
